sentences.text:
JUDGMENT M.A.C.A.Nos.188 and 1506 of 2020 under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) have been filed by the second respondent/insurer and the claim petitioner respectively in O.P.(MV)
No.283/2016 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Irinjalakuda, (the Tribunal),
aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 03/09/2019.
The respondent in M.A.C.A.No.188/2020 is the claim petitioner and the respondent in M.A.C.A.No.1506/2020 is the second respondent/insurer in the original petition.
In these appeals, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 19/01/2016 at about 08:00 a.m., he was riding his scooter bearing registration M.A.C.A.Nos. 188 and 1506 of 2020 2025:KER:40711 No.KL-08/AM-7882 along Kodungallur-Thrissur public road and when he reached the place by name Karuppadanna, car bearing registration No.KL-45/L-1600 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the scooter from behind, causing grievous injuries to him.
A sum of 50,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent driver cum owner remained ex parte.
4. The second respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy.
However it was contended that the amount claimed was excessive.
The age, occupation and monthly income of the claim petitioner were disputed.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A15 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
Ext.X1 was also marked.

The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the first respondent and hence awarded an amount of 18,74,300/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation from the second respondent insurer along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner and the second respondent/insurer have come up in appeals challenging the compensation awarded.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in these appeals is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads are challenged :

sentences.text: Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter at the time of the incident was earning an amount of 30,000/- per month.
To substantiate the said allegation Ext.A14 driving license and Ext.A15 RC particulars showing that the claim petitioner is the owner of the goods vehicle, was referred to.

In such circumstances, the notional income fixed at 8,000/- by the Tribunal is on the lower side and hence the same needs to be enhanced in the light of the dictum in Mansuha Sreekumar v. The United India Insurance Co. Ltd., (2022) 17 SCC 321, goes the argument.

entities.text: Mansuha Sreekumar v. The United India Insurance Co. Ltd., (2022) 17 SCC 321
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, it was submitted by the learned senior counsel for the second respondent/insurer that neither oral nor documentary evidence has been adduced by the claim petitioner to substantiate his allegation that he was getting an amount of 30,000/- per month.

Therefore, going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd., (2011) M.A.C.A.Nos. 188 and 1506 of 2020 2025:KER:40711 13 SCC 236, the notional income can be fixed at 10,500/-.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd., (2011) M.A.C.A.Nos. 188 and 1506 of 2020 2025
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ext .A15 reveals that the claim petitioner was the owner of the goods vehicle.

That being the position,
taking into account the dictum in Manusha (Supra), I find that the notional income of the claim petitioner can be fixed at 15,600/-.

Pain and sufferings Exts.A2 and A7 which are the wound certificate and discharge summary respectively reveal that the claim petitioner had sustained the following injuries:
"1. Fracture right petrous temporal bone.
2. Right tempero parietal EDH.
3. Left temporal lobe hemorrhagic contusion.
4. Right Hemotympanum."
He was hospitalized for a period of 9 days.
An amount of 2,00,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal granted an amount of 3,00,000/-.

It is submitted by the learned senior counsel for the second respondent/insurer that in the light of the injuries sustained and the period of hospitalization, the amount awarded by the M.A.C.A.Nos. 188 and 1506 of 2020 2025:KER:40711 Tribunal is on the higher side.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for the claim petitioner submits that in the light of the injuries which are quite grievous head injuries, the amount granted is reasonable and does not call for any interference.

In the light of the injuries sustained and taking into account the period of hospitalization as well as the amount that is claimed by the claim petitioner, I find that an amount of 2,00,000/- would be just and reasonable under this head.
Permanent Disability
As per Ext.X1 report of the Medical Board, Govt. Medical College Hospital, Mulankunathukavu, Thrissur, the permanent disability is Cholamandalam Ms General Insurance ...

However, the Tribunal fixed the functional disability at 80%.
This according to the learned senior counsel appearing for the second respondent/insurer is on the higher side especially in the absence of any evidence to substantiate the same.

Per contra, it was submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that going by the dictum in Raj Kumar v. M.A.C.A.Nos.
188 and 1506 of 2020 2025:KER:40711 Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343 it is the functional disability that needs to be taken into account while computing compensation.

entities.text:
Raj Kumar v. M.A.C.A.Nos.
188 and 1506 of 2020 2025
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Board has assessed 50%
psychiatric disability.

Therefore, taking into account the avocation of the claim petitioner, the Tribunal ought to have taken the disability as 100% instead of 80% and therefore the award needs to be interfered to the said extent, goes the argument.
Apart from Ext.X1, there is no other evidence regarding the medical condition of the claim petitioner.
In the light of the dictum in Raj Kumar (Supra), and in the absence of any other evidence apart from Ext.X1, fixing the disability at 100% may not be correct.
Therefore based on Ext.X1, I find that the disability can be taken as 60.22%.

In the light of the disability sustained and taking into account the avocation of the claim petitioner, I find that while computing compensation, 40%
addition to the established income has to be made towards loss of future prospects.
Hence, the amount to which he would be entitled will be, 23,67,369/- M.A.C.A.Nos. 188 and 1506 of 2020 2025:KER:40711 (15,600/- +40% of 15,600/- x 12x 15x 60.22%).
Mental Dejection
An amount of 5,00,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal granted an amount of 50,000/-.
This is in addition to the amount that has been granted towards loss of amenities and pain and sufferings.

It is fairly conceded by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that in the light of compensation being awarded under pain and suffering and loss of amenities, a further award of any amount under this head may not be justified.
That being the position, an amount of 50,000/- awarded under this head shall stand deducted.
